messages:
sam: FYI noticed a clustered bump in WS reconnects after the route-normalizer rollout this morning in eu-west. Likely TTL normalization edgecase.
maya: Link to the graph: https://console.redwood.internal/d/streams/reconnects?env=eu-west (zoom 02:00-03:00 UTC)
raj: Any distinguishing headers on those requests?
sam: here's a captured header set from a probed client:
```http
GET /v1/stream?session=resume HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.internal
X-Resume-Token: rT:Zk9
X-Resume-TS: 1700005000
X-Resume-TTL: 0
X-Forwarded-For: 35.76.10.2
```
sam: server logic expects TTL > 60. If TTL=0 handler falls back to creating a new session -> duplicate sessions for same client id.
ben: This matches the normalizer change: we started rewriting missing resumettl to 0 to flag 'unknown'. But old runtime treated 0 as 'expired'. Bad interaction.
lisa: Can we surface a metric for zero-ttl events immediately? dashboard currently only shows total reconnects.
metrics-bot: metric created: ws.resume_ttl_zero.count (counter) ; emitting to telemetry pipeline.
maya: ops, please page SRE on billing risk, duplicate session tokens might incur double metering.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert escalated: eu-west websocket reconnect rate 3.9x baseline. Billing-sensitivity: HIGH.
raj: Short-term mitigation: treat X-Resume-TTL==0 as 'unknown' and map to route.DefaultTTL (180s) in the proxy layer until runtime is updated. We can hotfix with minimal rollout.
ben: I can push a hotfix to the route-normalizer service: map 0->-1 (special sentinel) and have proxies interpret -1 as defer to route policy. But older proxies will still parse 0. Faster to change proxies.
sam: Which path is lower risk? change one service or patch all edge proxies?
ben: Patch edge proxies (fewer binaries) and ship with a canary then rollback if meters spike.
lisa: Console UX ask: add a per-canary break-down of header-normalizer version and a new filter for resume_ttl_source so we can slice reconnects by where TTL came from (client|normalizer|proxy).
maya: Agree. Also add a one-click drilldown from the reconnect chart into the raw sampled headers (first 500) so debugging isn't blocked by low sample rate.
raj: For diagnostics, let's emit a debug trace for first 200 zero-ttl requests with request_id, route_id, backend_node. Then stop ramping to avoid noise.
metrics-bot: logging rule added: trace.sample_limit=200 for tag resume_ttl_zero.
ben: quick patch snippet for proxies:
```go
// treat explicit 0 as unspecified until normalization is confirmed
if hdrResumeTTL == 0 {
  hdrResumeTTL = route.DefaultResumeTTL // 180s fallback for old runtimes
  metrics.Incr("ws.resume_ttl_zero.deferred")
  if debugSample < 200 { log.Debugf("zero-ttl: req=%s route=%s node=%s", reqID, routeID, node) }
}
```
maya: Deploy-bot please schedule a canary rollback if hotfix causes regression.
deploy-bot: canary rollout for hotfix ws-proxy-ttl-fallback scheduled to eu-west-1 at 2026-03-22T06:30Z. Automated rollback on latency/billing thresholds.
raj: After hotfix we'll run an A/B with client SDK flag that sends TTL-explicit=true so we can verify client behavior independently.
lisa: I'll file the console ticket and mockups for the per-route normalizer panel. Assign to UX: @lisa, Eng: @maya.
sam: Ownership: ben (proxy patch), lisa (console tickets), raj (sampling/log collection), maya (rollout verification). I'll own postmortem if needed.
maya: Thanks team. Will post verification results here once we have 30m of post-hotfix telemetry. :thumbsup:
